Instruction booklet

The server application _server: what it is for, what it answers, how to configure it

booklet/server-application2026-11-03Giovanni Porcari

Purpose

Every kajenn server carries one management application, _server (class ServerApplication, package kajenn.server_app). It is the system surface of the server: the login surface for humans, the management of users, credentials, tasks and databases, the monitor, the credential check that channels call, and three site documents (security.txt, robots.txt, favicon.ico).

This booklet states what _server does today on develop: why it exists, every route it answers and who may call it, every recipe word that configures it, how other code extends it, who uses it, and where its browser interface lives. Every fact carries its source.

Requirements

  • kajenn on develop after merge 3f5588d (2026-11-03).
  • For login and user management: an authentication().users(...) store in the recipe.
  • For OIDC: server(external_url=...) in the recipe.

Steps

1.Why it exists

kajenn keeps everything that asks a human for a user and a password out of the core. The core authenticates presented credentials through kajenn.auth and does not import kajenn.server_app; _server is the application that owns the login surface and the management routes, mounted like any other application.

ServerApplication extends OpenApiApplication, which extends RoutedApplication: its routes are ordinary routes with an OpenAPI description at /_server/_meta/schema_json.
readsrc/kajenn/server_app/server_app.py:2272026-11-03
code and mount are both _server, fixed on the class: PasswordMethod names /_server/login as its form action.

2.Know when it is mounted

A server always has _server. The recipe never declares it: it only customises it.

  • No application of code _server in the recipe or the kwargs → the server appends a default ServerApplication().
  • application(code="_server") without app_class → ServerApplication with the words written under it.
  • application(code="_server", app_class=MyServerApp) → accepted only when MyServerApp subclasses ServerApplication; otherwise the server refuses to build.
  • The dedicated process of an application declared with spawner="subprocess" mounts no _server: it hosts that application alone.
readsrc/kajenn/asgi_server.py:1382026-11-03
When the process has no role and no application has code _server, a default ServerApplication() is appended to the applications.
readsrc/kajenn/config/builder.py:902026-11-03
application(code="_server") without app_class takes ServerApplication.
readsrc/kajenn/config/handler.py:3092026-11-03
An app_class on code _server that is not a ServerApplication subclass raises ValueError naming the class.
testtests/core/test_server_app_always_present.py2026-11-03
A bare server, a recipe naming nothing and a recipe customising _server all mount it; the dedicated process of a spawned application mounts none.

3.Know what it answers and who may call it

Access is decided per route by its auth_rule: no identity answers 401, an identity without the tag answers 403. A route with an openapi_method refuses other methods with 405; a route without one answers every method.

Access summary
AccessRoutes
Public/_server/ (index), login, logout, login_methods, _meta/*, OIDC start and callback, the three well-known documents
KajennBus only (HTTP answers 403)auth/authenticate, auth/forget_credential
SUPERADMINusers/*, tokens/*, tasks/*
SERVER_ADMINmonitor/*, databases/*

The application itself

PathMethodWhat it does
/_server/anyDescriptor: {title, sections}, the attached section names.
/_server/loginPOSTidentity, password. Checks the lockout, verifies the password against the user store, attaches an Avatar to the current session. Answers {session_id, identity, tags}, or {error} with remaining_attempts for a known identity. Without a user store: "Login is not available".
/_server/logoutanyDeletes the session session_id; answers {"status": "ok"}.
/_server/login_methodsany{methods: [...]}: one descriptor per registered login method (id, kind, label, action), so a front-end draws the login screen without knowing the configuration.
/_server/_meta/schema_json, /_server/_meta/docs, /_server/_meta/indexanyOpenAPI 3.1 document, Swagger UI, HTML index (from OpenApiApplication).

PathMethodWhat it does
/_server/auth/authenticatePOST, bus onlycredential, channel. Verifies a presented credential through AuthCore; answers {identity, tags, data, valid_until}. It is the default authentication_route of every channel.
/_server/auth/forget_credentialPOST, bus onlyDrops a credential from the caches of every process.
/_server/auth/oidc:<code>/startanyStarts the OIDC authorization code flow with PKCE; 302 to the provider.
/_server/auth/oidc:<code>/callbackanyChecks the state, exchanges the code, verifies the id_token, attaches the avatar; 302 to the safe next path.

4.Configure it

The words of _server are written under its application element. The recipe customises it; it never has to declare it.

A recipe customising _server
Words of ServerApplicationGrammar
WordParametersEffect
loginmax_attempts (default 5), backoff seconds (default 30)Lockout after consecutive failures; the window doubles at each further failure.
oidc / providercode (required, the collection key), issuer, client_id, client_secret (a resolver; optional for a public client), scopes="openid email profile", identity_claim="email", tagsOne login method per provider, mounted at /_server/auth/oidc:<code>/.
security_txtcontact, expires (required); encryption, acknowledgments, preferred_languages, canonical, policy, hiring/.well-known/security.txt, validated at boot.
robots / agentsitemaps; per agent user_agent="*", allow, disallow/robots.txt, validated at boot.
parameters, request, databasesinherited from ApplicationGrammarAs for any application.

channels().channel(name, authentication_route=...)Replaces /_server/auth/authenticate for one channel.

5.Extend it

Another package adds routes to _server by attaching a section, and adds a login method by registering it. Both are public methods of ServerApplication.

MethodWhat it does
attach_section(section, name)Mounts a RoutingClass at /_server/<name>/ and lists it in sections and in the index.
sectionsThe attached sections by name.
register_auth_method(method)Adds a login method (kind form, redirect or ceremony); a duplicate id raises ValueError.
auth_section, ensure_auth_section()The auth section, created on first need.
app_snapshot, app_panel, panel_source on a sectionA section declaring them appears in the monitor as _server/<name>.
app_class subclass on code _serverReplaces the whole application with a subclass.

7.Find its browser interface

The browser interface of _server is not in kajenn. It lives in the repository kajenn-org/kajenn-serverapp-gui, today a placeholder holding the first version, built with gramlot and imported from a kajenn working tree. kajenn does not depend on gramlot.

The accepted proposal channels-meta-and-server-gui fixes the shape the GUI takes:

  • The recipe enables it with gui(gui_class=...); without the element there is no GUI and the core never names the package.
  • ServerApplication builds gui_class(self) and passes every request on ui/... to it: the URL is /_server/ui/. The component releases its resources in on_shutdown.
  • The GUI reads and writes only through the REST routes of _server, like any other client.
  • Extension pages register on the GUI component when it exists; gramlot is an optional extra of the extension.

The list of what the GUI must cover is in that repository, in xmldocs/proposal/server-gui-scope.xml.

Rules

must-not
Declare _server to make it exist.
The recipe customises _server; the server mounts it anyway.
must
Subclass ServerApplication when replacing _server through app_class.
The configuration handler refuses any other class.
must
Write server(external_url=...) when any OIDC provider is configured.
The server refuses to boot without it.
must-not
Import a GUI package from kajenn code.
kajenn does not depend on gramlot.
should
Give every GUI need a REST route on _server before building the page.
The proposal makes REST the only door of the GUI.

Current limits

The logout docstring says POST, but the route declares no method and answers every one; it has no auth_rule and deletes any session id it is given.
src/kajenn/server_app/server_app.py:538
The package docstring still says nothing is mounted automatically; the server mounts _server always. tests/server_app/test_config_server_app.py line 15 says the same.
src/kajenn/server_app/__init__.py:27
The monitor serves data only: no page. The per-application snapshot holds class, code and mount; pools, requests, websockets and databases are not in it.
src/kajenn/server_app/server_sections/monitor_section.py:27
With tasks disabled the tasks routes answer an error with status 200, not an error status.
src/kajenn/server_app/server_sections/tasks_section.py:52
No route reads or edits the effective configuration, the sessions, the logs or the application list with versions: a GUI cannot show them through REST today.
No route of _server declares a channel: the MCP face of the proposal is not there yet.
